description: Search a global professional database for people and get a sample of matches plus the true total match count. Ask with `filters` (recommended: state each part exactly, for example {"job_titles": ["M&A Associate", "Investment Banking Associate"], "locations": ["Frankfurt", "Munich"], "industries": ["Investment Banking"], "schools": ["University of Mannheim"]}) or with `query`, a plain-English sentence that is parsed for you (for example 'Heads of Marketing at Series B SaaS in New York'). Results are masked previews (a masked name, role, industry, company size and location) and each one carries an opaque `token`. Searching is FREE and spends no credits: use it to check that the right people come back before you pay, and refine the filters if they do not. To look up one named person, give `first_name` and `last_name` with their company or company domain when known. For a kind of employer no industry names exactly, use `company_keywords` (words its own description contains, for example ["hostel"] or ["SEO"] with industries ["Marketing Services"]). If nothing matches exactly, the search broadens itself: a job title is read more broadly first (`broadenedRole` gives the title as asked and as searched), then the least essential filters are dropped and `broadenedBy` names them; `ignored` lists any filter that could not be applied. To get a person's real name, LinkedIn and verified email, pass their token to reveal_profile, or use find_people with the same filters to unlock a batch in one call. It also works before a PeopleSearch.im account is connected: without one it returns up to 3 previews per search, up to 10 searches a day.

filters.description: Exact filters, recommended for AI agents and programs: state each part of the request instead of a sentence. Values inside one list are alternatives (OR); different fields must all match (AND). Give a few variants where people word things differently (titles: ["M&A Associate", "Investment Banking Associate"]). When filters are given, `query` is only a label and is not parsed.

companies.description: Current employers by name, e.g. ["Stripe"]. A name written with a legal form or a listing's tagline ("Stripe, Inc.", "Acme Pvt Ltd - Software House") is searched without it; for an exact company use company_domains or company_ids.

company_domains.description: Current employers by the website their LinkedIn company page lists, e.g. ["stripe.com"]. Exact for most companies, but some large ones list another site (Amazon's page lists aboutamazon.com, so amazon.com finds AWS staff), and a domain that hosts other organisations' pages (google.com) matches those organisations: check the company of the people returned.

company_ids.description: Current employers by their LinkedIn company page, the most exact way to name a company: the page's URL or its name in the URL, e.g. ["https://www.linkedin.com/company/google"] or ["google"], or LinkedIn's numeric company id. Use it for large companies, whose website often misses them (Google's page lists a short link, Amazon's lists aboutamazon.com).

company_keywords.description: Words the current employer's own description should contain, for a KIND of employer no industry names exactly, e.g. ["hostel"], ["coffee"] (founders of coffee roasteries), ["SEO"] (with industries ["Marketing Services"] for SEO agencies), ["community college"].

company_size_max.description: Maximum employees at the current employer.

company_size_min.description: Minimum employees at the current employer.

exclude_companies.description: Current employers to leave out, by name, e.g. ["Stripe"]. Needs another field to search by: with past_companies ["Stripe"] it finds former Stripe employees who no longer work there (11,810 of the 14,616 with Stripe in their past, measured 2026-10-19).

first_name.description: To find one named person: their first name, with the variants they may use, e.g. ["Timothy", "Tim"]. Use with last_name, and add companies or company_domains when known ("Anqi Dai at Memorial Sloan Kettering" finds the one person).

industries.description: Industry of the current employer, as LinkedIn names it, e.g. ["Investment Banking"], ["Software Development"], ["Hospitals and Health Care"], ["Venture Capital and Private Equity Principals"], ["Staffing and Recruiting"]. Common older names are mapped; a name that is not an industry is reported in `ignored` and not applied.

job_titles.description: Current job titles, matched as case-insensitive whole words ("Account Executive" also finds "Senior Account Executive"). Each is also searched in its other spellings ("CEO" and "Chief Executive Officer", "VP Sales" and "Vice President of Sales"). A bare "President" or "Owner" means the top job: Vice Presidents and Product Owners are left out unless you list such a title too. When nobody holds the titles, the same job under other titles is searched first (the company's President or Owner for "CEO"), reported in broadenedRole.

keywords.description: Words to find anywhere on the profile (headline, descriptions, past roles), for what no other field covers.

languages.description: Languages the person speaks, e.g. ["German"] or ["DE"].

last_name.description: To find one named person: their last name, e.g. ["Dai"]. If the name with the employer finds nobody, the search tries the last name at the employer, then the full name anywhere.

locations.description: Where the person lives or works: cities, states, countries or regions, e.g. ["Frankfurt", "Munich"], ["Germany"], ["DACH"], ["Texas"]. Use "City, Country" to tell same-named places apart ("Paris, France"). Country names are safest; ISO codes are converted.

past_companies.description: Former employers by name, e.g. ["McKinsey"] for ex-McKinsey people. Some people with a company in their past work there again or still: add the same names to exclude_companies for people who have left ("former employees of Stripe").

past_job_titles.description: Titles the person held before their current job.

schools.description: Schools the person attended, matched as substrings; add the local-language name too, e.g. ["University of Mannheim", "Universität Mannheim"].

skills.description: Skills listed on the profile, e.g. ["Python", "Kubernetes"].

years_experience_max.description: Maximum total years of professional experience.

years_experience_min.description: Minimum total years of professional experience.

limit.description: How many masked previews to return (1-25, default 10). This does not limit the reported total.

query.description: Who you are looking for, in plain English (role, seniority, industry, company, company size, location). Parsed for you. A company's website identifies it exactly, alone or in brackets after its name ('Head of Growth at Linear (linear.app)'). Optional when `filters` is given, where it is only a label.

name: people_search
title: Search people
